title: Spikes at the squares
credit: Cheon, Exner, Šeba (2000), arXiv:quant-ph/0004058 (continuum analogue with spikes at the squares).
results: Correct with a caveat. The spike gaps are 2m+1, so the spike-to-spike map is C·R(k(2m+1)), a one-frequency analytic cocycle over rotation by 2k. Herman's subharmonicity gives L ≥ log|C_11| = log sqrt(1+λ²/(4sin²k)). This bounds the phase-averaged exponent only: at the fixed phase θ=k (coupled to the frequency) the limit is not guaranteed, so eigenfunction decay is heuristic.
plain: On the half-line lattice, add a fixed spike of height λ at every perfect square. The free band (-2,2) then has no absolutely continuous spectrum, by Remling's theorem. Decide whether the spectrum inside the band is pure point (localized states) or singular continuous. A heuristic in the physics literature predicts singular continuous.
math: Let $(Hu)(n)=u(n+1)+u(n-1)+\lambda\,\mathbf 1_{\{m^2:m\ge1\}}(n)\,u(n)$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $u(0)=0$, $\lambda\ne0$ fixed, and let $\mu$ be the spectral measure of $\delta_1$. Determine the spectral type of $\mu|_{(-2,2)}$: is it pure point, purely singular continuous, or mixed? (Known: $\mu_{ac}=0$ by Remling's theorem. Cheon–Exner–Šeba heuristically predict purely singular continuous spectrum for the continuum analogue; positive Lyapunov exponents of the spike-to-spike cocycle suggest pure point.)
